Welcome to West Wimbledon Primary School
It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to West Wimbledon Primary School, a one-form entry primary school with a nursery for children aged 3-11, and a base for children with autism and social communication needs.
Our kind, nurturing and inclusive approach and our commitment to delivering an excellent curriculum ensures every child is able to reach his or her full potential. We strive to equip all our pupils with the confidence, resilience and knowledge they need to enjoy their learning now and in the future.
We are a wonderfully diverse community and our rich and varied curriculum is designed to ensure every pupil is able to identify with their learning and achieve.
We Work Hard
We set high expectations for all our pupils and expect all children to respect the right of every child to learn. The children understand that lesson time is for working and play time is for playing.
‘Leaders are ambitious for all pupils. They have carefully designed an ambitious, well-sequenced curriculum.’ OFSTED May 2022
We Are Kind
We greet each other with a smile every day and reinforce the power of being kind in everything we do.
‘Pupils develop into caring young people’ OFSTED May 2022
We Make Positive Choices
We adopt a positive approach at West Wimbledon to encourage independence and respect to all those in our community.
‘Pupils behave well in lessons, around the school and at playtimes’ OFSTED May 2022
We Show Pride
Our children are proud to come to school wearing the West Wimbledon logo. The children are proud of the progress they make and take care of our school and each other.
‘Pupils are proud of their school’ OFSTED May 2022
What Makes Us Special
Thanks are never enough for the amount of support your team give to my children. I count myself truly fortunate to have my children at your school. Both of my children now can't wait to go to school in the mornings...so different from when they started their educational journey. Parent Survey June 2026
‘We get to be ourselves’Y6 Pupil

pageCache.pageTitle: West Wimbledon Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Our mission
Aiming high to empower all children to thrive and become life-long learners.
Our high quality, ambitious and inclusive practice and curriculum ensures every child in our rich and diverse community is able to achieve and meet their full potential. Our belief, nurture and care towards every child supports them as individuals to succeed in a safe, loving and fair environment.
OUR VISION
Our vision is to enable all our pupils to reach their academic potential and to equip them with the knowledge and understanding which empowers them to become ambitious, happy and resilient learners. We strive to develop our pupils into compassionate and confident global citizens who celebrate differences and are empathetic and caring towards each other.
BELIEVE
We are a one-form entry, small community Primary school with a Nursery and a base for children with autism and communication needs and we believe in each and every child who comes through our door. We value every child and ensure they are able to learn and grow in an environment where they feel safe. We promise to respect each child’s individuality and we ensure that every child receives the positive encouragement and guidance essential to build self-esteem and develop independence. We believe every child can reach their potential, believe in themselves and follow their dreams.
ACHIEVE
At West Wimbledon Primary School, we enable all pupils to achieve, succeed and excel. We foster an environment where children not only achieve academically but are also encouraged to celebrate and recognise developments and successes in all areas of their personal growth. We nurture and help develop the children’s confidence and resilience to encourage them to become self-motivated individuals who are eager to learn and reach their goals. We strive to deliver a Curriculum which represents our diverse community and allows all our children to identify and engage with. Our goal is to instil a love and thirst for learning and to promote curiosity and interest now and in the future.
EMPOWER
We want all children to feel empowered and to use the knowledge they learn to make themselves heard. We want to empower our pupils to know that they can make a difference and with hard work and perseverance can achieve anything they put their minds to. We help all children to understand how they feel about themselves, their choices and their future at school and beyond. We are committed to empower our children to become the best they can be. We want all our children to feel confident and proud of themselves when they leave West Wimbledon Primary School and to feel excited and empowered to engage in the next stage of their learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: West Wimbledon Primary School - Welcome to Treetops
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Treetops
Our school is fortunate enough to include an Provision for children with Autism and social communication needs, which is called Treetops.
Treetops is one of six Primary ASC SEN Provisions within the Borough of Merton. We are one of five that are specifically for children who have Autism and social communication needs.
Pupils in Treetops will have and Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) with a primary need of social communication or autism.
Our pupils are primarily in the language and conversational partner stages of development in the SCERTS framework. This means they can use words and symbols to share thoughts and feelings, be able to engage in some form of reciprocal conversation and demonstrate an interest in others.
It is expected that pupils will access formal learning and the national curriculum, with specialist support.
Admissions to Treetops are entirely separate from places in the main school and are made through Merton’s Special Educational Needs Admissions Team. Joining the mainstream school will not advance admissions into Treetops or provide additional specialist support .
Teaching and Curriculum
Treetops is designed to provide a structured environment that is small, welcoming and inclusive. The staff strive to give pupils the maximum level of independence that they can achieve.
Class sizes are between 6 and 8 pupils, with a class teacher and between one and two teaching assistants. We have children from Reception through to Year 6, in mixed age classes (R/Y1, Y1/2, Y3/4, Y5/6).
All pupils have access to core subjects (Maths, English and Science) and the Foundation subjects (all other subjects). We use a topic-based approach to learning, which engages children and helps them to build skills in learning and thinking.
The method of teaching within the ARP is based on the principles of the Attention Autism Approach. This method strives to make learning engaging and motivating. The children are taught from the Early Years Foundation Stage and Primary National Curriculum, using a differentiated approach, adapted to the individual needs. We also use a carousel approach to support active participation, multimodal learning and collaboration.
In Treetops, we strive to enhance pupil’s social and emotional development, through specific PSHE and life skills sessions. We incorporate programmes such as Konnect, Social Thinking and the Zones of Regulation into daily practice. The pupils attend weekly swimming, horse riding and Creative Art lessons as part of an enriching curriculum.
Treetops Provision offer
Other professionals
Treetops has visiting Speech and Language therapists, who work onsite with the pupils. The children will have Speech and Language targets set twice per year, and a written report as part of their Annual Review. The Therapists and staff liaise closely regarding the pupils’ targets to ensure these are incorporated within daily teaching.
Treetops also has visiting Occupational Therapists, who work with children in a range of ways, which include both direct and indirect input. This enables OT programmes to be completed throughout the school day to support children’s access to their education. This ranges from scheduled movement breaks with specific exercises (e.g. sensory activities that range from low to high intensity depending on the child’s presenting needs), fine motor activities and resources to support writing skills. If your child has OT provision on their EHCP, you will receive Programmes and targets according to the amount outlined in Section F, as well as a written report as part of your child’s Annual Review.
Treetops works closely with Merton’s Educational Psychology team with an allocated Educational Psychologist. A referral may also be made if there is a change to your child’s needs or the provision that they require.
Access to mainstream lessons
The School is also committed to adopting an inclusive approach in all aspects of its work. We believe that where it is suitable for an individual learner in Treetops, access to mainstream classes can help to promote independence and social awareness. This can take several forms: shared playtimes, lunchtimes, assemblies, residential trips as well participate in selected mainstream lessons. All mainstream opportunities are planned for on an individual basis to ensure these experiences are both meaningful and beneficial for the child. Not all pupils will take part in mainstream sessions. Treetops is part of the main School building: not set apart from it and we seek to ensure that our practice reflects that geography.
Assessment
We assess Treetops learners using the greater precision offered by a system called Connecting Steps, from BSquared. It is better configured to record the smaller steps of progress that our learners make, to build a bigger and more accurate picture of each pupil’s learning and progress.
We use the SCERTS Model framework to assess social and emotional learning. This is used to create a profile of your child’s social and emotional competencies and highlight priorities for further development. As part of this, you will be asked to complete a form about your child’s social communication and emotional regulation at home. For each child, a SEN support plan is in place. This SEN support plan draws on the outcomes outlined in pupil’s EHCPs, the SCERTS profile and BSquared assessment. The targets are devised and reviewed in consultation with parents, on a termly basis.
Communication with parents
We believe collaboration with parents and carers is key to ensuring the best possible outcomes for pupils. We start the year with a ‘Meet the Teacher’ session to introduce you to your child’s teacher for the year, as well as gain an understanding of the expectations of the upcoming year. In addition to the statutory Education, Health and Care Plan Annual Review meeting, two parent meetings are held to discuss each child’s progress. There is also an opportunity to talk through your child’s end of year report. We also use Communication Diaries to provide an opportunity for parents and staff to communicate on a regular basis. We also welcome parents and carers to telephone or email the school. Each parent will be able to create an Evisense login to access photos and observations of their child in school.

Welcome
'Believe, Achieve, Empower' are three core words which are so important to us at West Wimbledon and integral to our vision and values for all our children.
Believe - We simply believe in every child and help them to reach their full potential and goals. To do this, each child must believe in themselves. We commit to making our school an engaging, fun and safe place to learn and play. At West Wimbledon we want all children to feel a true sense of belonging and know that it is their school where they can shine, make mistakes and feel happy.
Achieve - We foster an environment where children not only achieve academically but where they are also encouraged to celebrate and recognise developments and successes in all areas of their personal growth. We pride ourselves on our excellent attainment outcomes. In May 2026, the proportion of our Year 6 mainstream children achieving the higher standard in reading, writing and maths was above the national average and 96% of our mainstream Year 1 pupils met the expected standard in their phonics screening check.
Empower - We empower our children to use their new learning and knowledge in order to be heard. We help all children to understand how they feel about themselves, their choices and their future at school and beyond. We are committed to empowering our children to become the best they can be. We want all our children to feel confident and proud of themselves when they leave West Wimbledon Primary School and to feel excited and empowered to engage in the next stage of their learning.
Please navigate around this site to discover what makes us so popular with local families, and to stay informed of the range of curriculum approaches and extra-curricular activities we offer.
If you are a prospective parent, please come and visit our school by booking onto one of our regular tours – the dates can be found here.
I couldn’t be more proud to be the Head teacher of this beautiful school where we get to know every single child as an individual.
We very much look forward to welcoming you to West Wimbledon in person soon, and demonstrate our commitment to providing local children with the highest quality of education, and the best possible start in their educational careers.With very best wishes, Mrs Rosie Williamsonheadteacher@westwimbledon.merton.sch.ukHeadteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: West Wimbledon Primary School - Breakfast Club
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
The West Wimbledon Primary School Breakfast Club takes place in the Hut and is run by school staff. It is open to children at our school from Reception to Year 6.
Breakfast Club opens at 7.45am and children may arrive at any time after that. Children are taken to their class lines in time for the morning school bell at the start of the school day.
Places in our Breakfast Club are limited and must be booked through Arbor and paid for in advance.
The cost of a place at Breakfast Club is currently £4.50 per child per day. This will be reviewed annually. The children are provided with a range of breakfast cereals, toast, bagels, pancakes, fruit, juice and milk.
Play and education-related resources are made available to the children and games and craft activities are organised and led by our staff.

pageCache.pageTitle: West Wimbledon Primary School - Music Tuition
pageCache.text:
Music Tuition
Tuition is given by experienced tutors either at West Wimbledon Primary School or at Merton Music Centre.
The choice of instruments offered at each school depends on the number of pupils who apply. If the instrument you require is not currently taught at West Wimbledon Primary School you may apply directly to Merton Music Centre for lessons outside school hours. Group, shared or individual lessons may be requested, and there are choices for the length of lessons. Pupils generally start with group lessons of between three and six pupils depending on the type of instrument. More advanced pupils progress to tuition on a shared or individual basis.
MMF offers tuition across the full range of instruments:
On site tuition is available for piano, violin and guitar only, at this point in time: due to current parental demand. A greater range of instrument tuition might be available within school should a sufficient number of West Wimbledon parents choose a particular instrument.
Merton Music Foundation’s website now makes it even easier to find out information about the instruments taught, the cost and what else might be available.
Children are usually taught on a rota basis so they don’t miss the same lessons each week.
The School is very fortunate to work in partnership with Merton Music Foundation (MMF).

pageCache.pageTitle: West Wimbledon Primary School - Trips and Excursions
pageCache.text:
Trips and Excursions
At West Wimbledon Primary School, we seek to ensure that the National Curriculum is delivered to all children, regardless of social background, race, gender or differences in ability.
All are entitled to the development of knowledge, understanding, skills, and attitude. To enrich the curriculum for our children we also offer a wide range of educational visits and other activities that add to what is learned in school.
The School has adopted the Merton outdoor educational handbook ‘There and Back Again’ which gives advice and guidance on planning a visit/residential.
In the summer term, our Year 5 are offered a 5 day residential visit to the Kingswood Centre on the Isle of Wight. A presentation and information are given to parents each year explaining the school trip and what the children can expect.
PLANNING FOR SUCCESSFUL TRIPS AND EXCURSIONS
Learning outside school is a valuable addition to the children’s educational experience. The School has a comprehensive Educational Visits policy which is always followed. Its purpose is to ensure the safety of the children and adults during the visit through careful planning and to identify and manage potential risks, so that the children derive the maximum educational value and enjoyment from the visit.
To view the Educational Visits Policy please see the ‘Our Policies’ section of this website.

pageCache.text:
After School Club: The Hideout
The School runs a highly popular after-school childcare provision in the Hut for children in Reception to Year 6 (named by the children as Hideout).
The hours of the provision’s operation are 15:30 – 18:00
Families of current West Wimbledon Primary School pupils who are interested in seeking a place are requested to complete the Hideout Application Form and return it to the School as soon as possible, as places are always allocated on a first come, first serve basis. Forms may be handed in to the School office or e-mailed to school@westwimbledon.merton.sch.uk. Information on the provision and details of how to apply may be found in the documents below.
Bookings for Hideout are made through Arbor.
Hideout New User Application Form
Terms and Conditions - After School Club Provision
The fee for Hideout is £15.00 per pupil per day. This will be reviewed annually.

Clubs
We have a wide range of after-school clubs and activities available
Please use the link below to view the list of clubs running.
Clubs: Autumn Term 2026
Parents and carers can reserve a club place by booking and paying for a space on Arbor and completing a club collection arrangements form. For children who are eligible for pupil premium, a free club space can be reserved by phoning the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: West Wimbledon Primary School - Literature Wishlist
pageCache.text:
Literature Wishlist
At WWPS we strive to foster a love of reading and a passion for books! In order to get children excited about and enjoying books from a wide range of genres and authors, it is important to keep our book corners and libraries current and fresh. New and exciting books are being published all the time and our children are always keen to get stuck into new releases! With this in mind, we have set up 2 Amazon Wishlists. The first is for phase 1 (year 1-3) and the second is for phase 2 (year 3-6). If you would like, and are able, to donate a book to the school, please click on the links below. Once you have added a book to your basket, it should give you the option of sending this to the school as a gift. Please ensure you complete the gift note so that we know who has kindly bought the book.

pageCache.pageTitle: West Wimbledon Primary School - Special Education Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
pageCache.text:
Special Education Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
At West Wimbledon Primary School, we pride ourselves on being a welcoming inclusive environment for all children.
We strive to remove barriers to learning, to enable all pupils to achieve equitably and participate fully at school. In order to do this, many steps are taken to support pupils in their learning. We maintain a primary focus on high quality inclusive classroom teaching so that all children can reach at least age-expected levels. However, for some children, additional support is needed to help them achieve this.
The 2014 Code of Practice says: “A child or young person has special educational needs if he or she has a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special educational provision to be made for him or her. A learning difficulty or disability is a significantly greater difficulty in learning than the majority of others of the same age. Special educational provision means educational or training provision that is additional to, or different from, that made generally for others in a mainstream setting in England.”
Children with SEN will have needs and requirements that fall into at least one of the following four areas:

pageCache.pageTitle: West Wimbledon Primary School - Curriculum in Treetops
pageCache.text:
Curriculum in Treetops
Treetops Curriculum Overviews for the whole year:
Intent
To provide a caring, inclusive and holistic learning environment that sits at the heart of its community and provides a high level of challenge, stimulation and support. We are committed to enabling each child to maximise her/his potential for both academic and personal successes – which we characterise in our motto: Aiming High.
Aiming High
A holistic approach to teaching and learning is a fundamental principle within Treetops. We aim to address the emotional, social, and academic needs of pupils in an integrated learning format. Emphasis is placed on positive school environments and providing whole-child supports (academic and non-academic) to enable children to thrive. Children’s attainment and progress outcomes are guided by pupils’ individual needs. Alongside high expectations we consider children’s personal, social and sensory profiles, in order to recognise the achievements of each child. Children’s social and emotional development and opportunities for independence are carefully planned for, based on their individual strengths and needs. The curriculum in Treetops is designed with the needs of our pupils at its heart. It is underpinned by the teaching of functional skills and key knowledge based on the primary national curriculum, with a focus on communication, social and emotional learning. Children’s learning is based upon their developmental level to ensure progression is attainable and meaningful.
Implementation
Language and communication underpin the curriculum in Treetops. We are committed to provide learning opportunities and an environment that promotes and develops children’s language and communication skills, therefore the majority of our lessons are delivered through the Attention Autism programme by Gina Davies. This ensures learning is engaging and motivating, as well as accessible and targeted. We also use a carousel approach to support active participation, multimodal learning and collaboration. We work collaboratively to provide a curriculum whereby the academic demands are supported by Speech and Language Therapy and Occupational Therapy.
Maths: Our Maths curriculum is based on the Maths mastery ‘White Rose Scheme’. We use the Concrete, Pictorial, Abstract (CPA) approach that develops a deeper understanding of maths in pupils.
Writing: Our English curriculum is based on the ‘Drawing Club' Approach. Drawing Club incorporates story sharing, speaking and listening, drawing, writing, vocabulary, imagination and collaboration. The approach enables teachers to immerse children in the world of story, develop creativity, be child/ interest-led which enables children to progress and feel success in writing which is often a challenging subject for our learners.
Reading: We use the ‘Read, Write, Inc’ Programme in the teaching of phonics to support the development of reading and spelling skills. Some pupils also follow the Literacy and Language programme to support the development of reading comprehension; spelling, punctuation and grammar.
Handwriting: In the first instance we follow the handwriting programme by ‘Read, Write, Inc’. We also use a range of handwriting programmes based on pupils' individual needs and occupational therapy recommendations such as ‘Handwriting without Tears’, ‘Write from the Start’ and ‘Speed it up!’.
Geography and History: As we follow a topic-based curriculum, the focus of the Geography and History units are reflected across the curriculum. The units focus on key concepts and skills to develop children’s understanding of place, civilization, similarity and difference, diversity, using sources of information and evidence.
Social and Emotional Learning: Our curriculum has a strong focus on social and emotional learning. We use a range of programmes to support the teaching of these areas including the ‘Social Thinking Programme’ (We Thinkers, Social Detectives, Superflex), ‘PECS So Safe’ and the ‘Zones of Regulation’.
PE: The PE curriculum includes weekly sessions focused on basic movement skills, participation in team games and performances. Children also attend swimming and horse riding lessons for half the school year, both supporting the development of life skills and core stability and strength, key occupational therapy needs for many pupils.
Art, Drama and DT: Our Creative Art teacher, delivers weekly sessions during which they are able to explore and learn different forms of expression including drama and dance.
Computing - Our curriculum develops children’s understanding of how to keep themselves safe online, to become IT literate, computational thinking and make links to everyday life.
Impact
As a result of our teaching and curriculum in Treetops you will see children who are:
engaged and motivated in their learning

Our Governors
The Governors at West Wimbledon work in partnership with Merton Council and the school community to provide the best possible education for the children at the school.
The Governing Body comprises thirteen governor positions. When required, new governors are appointed based on the added value of the skills and experience they bring to the governing body. We currently have three vacancies and welcome expressions of interest from individuals who would like to contribute to the strategic leadership and continued success of the school.
Parents, former parents, community volunteers, staff and local business people are represented on the governing body. The governing body meets formally as a whole committee at least four times a year, and each of our four committees (Standards; Teaching and Learning; Pupils and Community; and HR and School Business) meets once a term. All governors also visit the school regularly to inform their work and monitor their focus areas.

TIMES OF THE SCHOOL DAY
8:40 – 8:50 – The school gates open for all children. Children can go straight to class – no lining up. Nursery parents and Reception parents during the first term, are able to accompany their child to the classroom door.
8:50 – The school gates and entrance doors will be locked. Children arriving after 8:50 will need to enter the school via the main school reception area.
11:40 – End of the day for Morning Nursery children.
12:30 – Afternoon Nursery children arrive.
12.30 – 13:30 – Lunch
15.15 – 15.30 – Staggered end of day as follows:
15.15 – Treetops children
15:20 - Reception and Year 1
15:25 - Years 2 and 3
15:30 - Nursery and Years 4-6
ATTENDANCE
It is vital that children attend school every day, and only ever miss time if illness or other emergency circumstances make it completely impossible for them to come in. The expectation at West Wimbledon Primary School is clear: that every child is in school every day.
If your child is not well enough to come to school, please telephone the office on 0208 946 1620 by 09.30, to give the reason for absence and when your child is expected to return to school.
The School would like to take this opportunity to remind parents that family holidays must not to be taken during term time.
